isolation: The catalogue (library-service) is static, seeded once at startup and read-only for the life of the deployment (specs/design/components/library-service/design.json: 'static in-memory data seeded at startup... never accepts a write') -- nothing is created per scenario. Every Given was verified by reading the CURRENT catalogue straight from library-service's own intranet-only endpoint, reached over the cluster network this run has from its pod (http://ai-agent-bookbuddy-library-service.dp-default-ai-agent-book-development-4c85f106.svc.cluster.local:9090/books), which is read-only and never mutated by any route, so each read is sound regardless of what else runs concurrently. No scenario reached its When: book-buddy is this project's only interface (type ai-agent, no web-application component exists in this project; design.json: exposesAPI.auth 'end-user-required') and its PRD states it is 'reached through the standard /chat interface via the Try it test app' -- a platform console whose registered redirect_uri (http://tryit.ae.localhost:8080/callback, published on the roles-gate ticket #3) is a localhost address unreachable from this run. Completing the OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE sign-in that interface requires needs this project's registered OAuth client_id, which the platform only ever publishes into a web app's window._env_ (thunder-authentication skill) -- and this project has no web app to carry it. The client_id is not in the validation issue, not in /tmp/validation-context.json, not on the roles-gate ticket, not on any reachable endpoint, and the IdP's dynamic client registration endpoint refuses an unauthenticated registration attempt with unauthorized_client (admin auth required). This run additionally tried, and ruled out, two routes a prior validation attempt had not: (1) the IdP's advertised grant types (client_credentials, authorization_code, refresh_token, token-exchange, ciba, jwt-bearer) include no resource-owner-password grant, so the test user's published username/password cannot be exchanged for a token without a client_id either way; (2) book-buddy's own in-cluster Service was reached directly, bypassing the public API gateway entirely, and it answered /chat with its own 401 (empty body, distinct from the gateway's JSON 401) -- book-buddy validates the bearer itself against USER_AUTH_JWKS_URL rather than trusting an upstream gateway header, so bypassing the gateway does not bypass authentication. Every avenue this run could reach ends at the same missing client_id.
